items.title: Faster palette handling
items.text: Colour palettes are expanded, looked up and hashed with less CPU work, and the last palette and pipeline lookup are reused when nothing changed.

items.title: Faster texture lookups
items.text: Looking up textures costs fewer CPU cycles: blocks of graphics memory now get a cheap identity instead of being hashed again and again, and the app picks the fastest method for the device the first time it is used. Clears of whole pages also keep their identity, which helps games such as MotoGP.

items.title: Less bookkeeping per graphics draw
items.text: Several per-draw checks in the graphics thread, such as finding the target and clearing out invalidated sources, are now skipped or cached when nothing changed. Large clears of 24-bit or masked memory also use fewer instructions.

items.title: Faster vertex processing
items.text: The graphics thread spends less CPU time turning game geometry into draws. This helps games that send many small sprites or triangles, such as Call of Duty 3 and Sly 3.

items.title: Repeated copy draws are skipped
items.text: Games that repeat the same copy-style draws, such as Spider-Man 3, now skip the repeats once they have been recorded, which saves graphics thread time. It is on by default with no setting, and pictures are identical with it on or off.

items.title: Faster graphics readbacks
items.text: Games that read the screen back to the CPU, such as Metal Gear Solid 3, SOCOM II and The Punisher, wait less: several reads now share one trip to the GPU, results are written back a block at a time, and the CPU waits for each answer more efficiently.

items.title: Depth buffer moves stay on the GPU
items.text: Elemental Gelade moves its frame into the next frame's depth buffer once a frame. That move now stays on the GPU, and the moved data is kept until memory is read or written there.

items.title: Fewer reads for alpha masked draws
items.text: Draws that hold back alpha bits read their target less often, because the renderer now tracks which alpha bits are already known inside parts of a target and tests destination alpha in the shader when it can.

items.title: Faster texture pack loading
items.text: Texture packs decode faster: BC7 textures are interpolated with vector instructions and JPEG textures are decoded straight to RGBA.

items.title: Faster in-game video decoding
items.text: The decoder behind in-game movies now does all rows and columns of its inverse DCT at once with vector instructions, and gives the same output as before.

items.title: Bigger graphics upload buffers
items.text: Large image uploads no longer fill the graphics upload buffers and make the CPU wait on the graphics. The buffers are now 32 MB on devices with 2 GB of RAM or more, and they keep their size when you load a save state.

items.title: Lower memory use for VU jump tables
items.text: Large lookup tables used by the vector unit recompiler are now set up lazily, so parts a game never reaches no longer take up memory.

items.title: Software renderer handles extreme texture values
items.text: The software renderer now treats extreme texture coordinate values the way the console does, based on measurements from an SCPH-30001 console, and keeps the values as the game sent them.

items.title: Fix a crash on an empty VIF1 read
items.text: A game reading from the empty VIF1 queue no longer aborts a release build. It now gets zeroes and a warning, as the console would. One bug report hit this after 73 minutes of play.

items.title: Software renderer glitch fixes
items.text: The software renderer no longer refills a texture while a queued draw still reads it, and no longer splits a draw across workers when its frame and depth buffers share memory pages. Both could produce wrong pixels.

items.title: Fix a graphics buffer memory leak
items.text: Resetting the graphics draw buffers now frees the old ones, which fixes a leak of about 2.2 MiB on every reset. Very large vertex buffers also fail with a clear error instead of wrapping around.

items.title: Extended RAM works with the recompiler
items.text: Extended RAM, which gives the PS2 128 MB of main memory as on a development console, can now be used with the ARM64 recompiler outside arcade sessions. Homebrew, prototypes and game patches that need more memory rely on it.

items.title: Fix VU0 access to VU1 registers
items.text: VU0 programs that reach VU1's registers now work out the address when they run, so they stay correct when saved code is reused.

items.title: Fix a crash when starting a new game
items.text: Fixed a crash that could happen at the start of a new session when MTVU was on and the previous session had left VU1 marked as running.

items.title: Stuntman and Driv3r AI stays on route
items.text: Every Stuntman and Driv3r version now uses Full floating point clamping in its game settings, which fixes the AI drivers leaving their routes.

items.title: Hidden virtual pad stays hidden
items.text: A virtual pad you hid stays hidden after you open and close the menu. Before, the pad came back.

items.title: Speed shortcut remembers live speed
items.text: After a trip to the menu, the speed shortcut keeps stepping from the speed the game is really running at instead of from the saved speed.

items.title: Renamed games stay in place on favorite
items.text: Renamed games stay in their sorted place when you favorite or unfavorite them, instead of jumping to where their file name would sort until the next scan.

items.title: Saved themes keep orientation options
items.text: A saved Game Library theme now stores the right fallback for an orientation option you never set, so the theme loads the way it looked.

items.title: Library decides landscape in one place
items.text: The Game Library now decides portrait or landscape from one place, so card settings, layout and the launch animation no longer disagree in some window sizes.

items.title: Long press opens card menu reliably
items.text: A long press on a library card no longer sometimes boots the game instead of opening its context menu, which could happen after a rotation.

items.title: Settings Version row opens About
items.text: The Version row in the Settings list now opens the About page, the same way Licenses and Help open their pages.

items.title: JIT starts on more devices
items.text: JIT, the mode that lets games run at full speed, now starts on A12 to A14 devices running iOS 26, which do not need to wait for the StikDebug handshake. On Dopamine 2.1 and later, the app also asks to be marked as debugged at launch.

items.title: Safer JIT check and honest status
items.text: The app now runs a tiny test routine from JIT memory before relying on it, so a device that cannot run its own generated code is caught early instead of crashing in the first game block. Settings also shows JIT Off while the interpreter is running, instead of JIT Access Detected.
